sample_unit: patient queries from a public forum (each answered by 3 chatbots and a surgeon)

links.outcome: Flesch reading ease/grade level of AI chatbot responses versus physician responses
links.effect: Reading ease was greater for surgeon responses (60.6; grades 8-9) than Perplexity (40.0, college) and ChatGPT (35.5, college) (P<.01).
links.quote: Reading ease was greater for the minimally invasive gynecologic surgeon responses (60.6 [53.5-68.4]; eighth and ninth grade) than for Perplexity (40.0 [28.6-47.2], college) and ChatGPT (35.5 [28.2-42.0], college) (P<.01).

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot patient-facing responses versus general population health literacy
links.effect: Perplexity and ChatGPT responses were at college reading level vs 8th-9th grade for the surgeon (P<.01); readability must reflect general population health literacy.
links.quote: Reading ease was greater for the minimally invasive gynecologic surgeon responses (60.6 [53.5-68.4]; eighth and ninth grade) than for Perplexity (40.0 [28.6-47.2], college) and ChatGPT (35.5 [28.2-42.0], college) (P<.01).

links.outcome: Physician-rated quality and accuracy of chatbot responses versus surgeon
links.effect: Doximity GPT and ChatGPT had quality and accuracy similar to the surgeon; Perplexity was significantly worse for quality and accuracy (P<.001).
links.quote: There was a significant difference between Perplexity and the other response sources, favoring the latter, for quality and accuracy (P<.001).

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, empathy, understandability, and readability of responses to postoperative patient queries generated by several LLM chatbots compared with a physician, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
